lines.text: ## Grouping rules
- Group by review concern: why these hunks are read together. A directory qualifies only when that directory is the concern.

- A group is one concern a reviewer names in a phrase. The code, the unit tests that check it, and the one-line call sites, declarations, and re-exports that serve it read together in that group; the digest `pairs with` hint names a test's module. A new integration harness is the concern: that harness and the build or CI files that run it are one group, not the production group they exercise. A new feature's code, fixtures, seeds, helpers, and the spec that runs them are one group. A foundation split is for a contract several later groups share. Split a concern only where a reader would stop and review the first piece alone. A `trivial` or `small` review has one to three groups.

- A group is one concern a reviewer names in a phrase. The code, the unit tests that check it, and the one-line call sites, declarations, and re-exports that serve it read together in that group; the digest `pairs with` hint names a test's module. A new integration harness is the concern: that harness and the build or CI files that run it are one group, not the production group they exercise. A new feature's code, fixtures, seeds, helpers, and the spec that runs them are one group. A foundation split is for a contract several later groups share. Split a concern only where a reader would stop and review the first piece alone.
- A hunk may appear in several groups when it matters in more than one story. When one hunk holds two concerns, the group that holds it names both.

- `dependsOn` marks a real dependency inside one story: the reader needs the earlier group to understand this one. It stays inside one part. Reading order inside a story: contracts and foundations, then call sites, then mechanical work. Independent work stands alone with its own `part` and empty `dependsOn`. A second feature, extra product events, a dependency policy change, or standalone documentation that could have been its own PR is independent work. Unasked work that only enables the asked story (path renames, fixture layout, local startup) stays one part with that story, or one harness part. Two concerns share a `part` when the asked story needs both; otherwise they are separate parts.
- `part` is a short name (a few words) for one independent story, the same on every group in that story; the UI colors shared parts together. One document `parts[]` entry per name.
